case.summary: Transaction 3478561 ($74.96, online, 2016-11-22) was flagged as part of an analyst review of coordinated fraud across multiple cards. Graph analysis identified that the specific device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M, Android 7.0) used for this transaction is appearing as a new device across 28 different cardholders within one month, all behind an anonymous proxy, indicating a single fraudulent origin rather than a compromised individual account. This undocumented pattern does not fit the five established fraud signatures but matches the structural characteristics of six prior closed cases, all confirmed fraud with total exposure of $3,601.87. The cardholder's baseline activity (85 transactions, median $48.03, across 2 regions and multiple channels) shows no signs of compromise. Fraud probability is assessed at 0.90 with high confidence. The flagged transaction will be declined and the card blocked pending further investigation of the connected device cluster.

sar.narrative: Customer C13487 holds card C13487-K1, which was used to make a $74.96 online purchase of product code C on November 22, 2016 at 16:11 UTC in billing region 191.0. The transaction originated from a device with the specific profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M running Android 7.0 and Chrome 62.0 for Android at 1920x1080 resolution, routed through an anonymous proxy. This device profile is marked as new to the account. The same device profile was used by 28 different cardholders within a one-month window, with each instance appearing as a new device on the respective accounts and each routed through an anonymous proxy. This pattern does not match any of the five documented fraud patterns because it represents coordinated abuse from a single origin across multiple unrelated cardholders rather than compromise of any individual account. Eight prior closed cases retrieved as structurally similar, all confirmed as fraud, show total exposures of $3,601.87. The bank's model risk score for this transaction was 0.05, which is a low input signal on its own. The activity is suspicious because a specific handset build simultaneously appears as new across dozens of unrelated accounts behind anonymous routing, indicating systematic card testing or fraud originating from a single coordinated source rather than legitimate cardholder activity. The bank created a case, escalated to analyst review, monitored connected cards, and filed a report with total suspicious exposure of $74.96 on this flagged transaction.
